titulo: The maha mantra, on a Thursday
caption:
Hare Krishna Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna Hare Hare, Hare Rama Hare Rama, Rama Rama Hare Hare.
Per Prabhupada: Hare calls the energy of the Lord, “like the genuine cry of a child for its mother”; Krishna and Rama both mean the supreme pleasure.
Link in bio.
by NMR
#harekrishna #mantra #bhakti

alt.1: amber field, Cella saying “Spiritual? Moi?” in a speech bubble. Hare Krishna, Hare Rama. In 3 ordinary moments. Three words. Your 3 a.m. self already knows them.
alt.2: dark blue field at night, a pale yellow Cella next to a phone, saying “Mom?”. Hare: a call to the energy of the Lord, like a child crying for its mother. Everyone calls someone at 3 a.m. Be honest about who.
alt.3: coral field, Cella with her eyes shut laughing “Ha ha ha HA” next to a phone. Krishna: the supreme pleasure. You laughed till it hurt. Nobody paid you.
alt.4: green field, Cella with her eyes shut next to a sofa, saying “No plans.”. Rama: the supreme pleasure, again: two names for it. Sunday, no plans, no reason. You keep calling it luck.
alt.5: the three words as a list. The maha mantra, per Prabhupada (1966): Send it to whoever you call at 3 a.m. 1. Hare · the call. 3 a.m. counts. 2. Krishna · the supreme pleasure. 3. Rama · same pleasure, second name.
